title: AES-GCM engine with an AXI4 DMA: AAD and text read from memory, the output text written back, tag in registers
features: The unchanged AES_GCM_top core (AES-128 / AES-256, 96-bit IV, NIST SP 800-38D).
Source: AAD_LEN bytes of AAD padded with zeros to 16 bytes, then TXT_LEN bytes of text; byte 0 of a block is the lowest address.
The output text goes to DST_ADDR, rounded up to 16 bytes with zero padding.
Decrypt: the plaintext is written before the tag is checked; use it only when STATUS.tag_ok is 1.
Two copies of the shared AXI4 engine, one for reads and one for writes, on one manager port.

fields.desc: 0 the KEY registers, 1 the sideload key port
decrypt: bytes of TAG_IN compared (the first ones), 0 = 16

regs.name: KEY
regs.desc: Key, 256 bits over eight write-only words (KEY7 holds bits 255:224, the first key bytes; AES-128 uses KEY7..KEY4); reads return 0

regs.name: IV
regs.desc: 96-bit IV over three words (IV2 holds bits 95:64, the first IV bytes)

regs.name: TAG_IN
regs.desc: Decrypt: the expected tag over four words (TAG_IN3 holds bits 127:96, the first tag bytes); compared when the message ends

fields.desc: expected tag, big-endian, left-aligned when truncated
start a job; ignored while busy

regs.name: STATUS
regs.desc: Job state and result (cleared by start)

fields.desc: the current / last job saw an AXI error response
core error cause: 1 format, 2 order, 3 too long, 4 sideload key not valid

regs.name: TAG
regs.desc: Encrypt: the 128-bit tag (TAG3 holds bits 127:96, the first tag bytes); 0 after a decryption

fields.desc: authentication tag of the last encryption
clocks from start to DONE of the current / last job

irqs.name: ERR
irqs.desc: a job ended with an AXI or core error

sequence: Write CTRL, KEY, IV (and TAG_IN when decrypting).
Write SRC_ADDR, DST_ADDR (word aligned) and LEN.
Wait for irq; read TAG (encrypt) or STATUS.tag_ok (decrypt); write 1s to IRQ_STATUS.
notes: sl_key / sl_valid are the sideload key port of the core (CTRL.key_sel = 1); they pass through unchanged.

m_* is the AXI4 manager port (32-bit address and data, 4-bit ID, no user / QoS); it passes through unchanged. Bursts are INCR, AxSIZE = 2 (4 bytes), 1 to 16 beats, WSTRB = 4'hF, never across a 4 KB boundary; one read and one write burst are outstanding at a time. A read burst is issued only when its data has room, a write burst only when all its data is ready.
